views.name: classroom_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,
  classroom.capacity AS capacity
FROM classroom

params.description: Provides one row per physical classroom (building + room_number) with its seating capacity.
params.when_to_use: Lookup the capacity for a specific classroom (by building and room_number). | Build higher-level aggregations of classroom counts or total capacity per building or campus when composed with aggregation. | Compose into schedules or resource planning queries that need classroom identifiers with their capacity as a base attribute.
params.output_schema: building: identifier of the building that contains the classroom; derived directly from classroom.building | room_number: identifier of the room within the building; derived directly from classroom.room_number | capacity: seating capacity (or defined capacity) of the classroom; derived directly from classroom.capacity
params.metric: capacity = classroom.capacity (base attribute, not an aggregate or computed metric)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a building-level dimension (e.g., a view keyed by building) on building — safe because classroom_base is one-row-per (building, room_number). Joining to one-row-per-building will not duplicate capacity measures when the planner treats classroom_base rows individually or aggregates classroom_base first. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a room-level dimension keyed by (building, room_number) — safe because both sides are one-row-per-room and will not duplicate measures. | do NOT join directly to any one-to-many table/view (for example: a reservations or class_schedule table with multiple rows per classroom) without re-aggregating the many-side first or aggregating classroom_base after the join, because such a join will multiply classroom_base rows and thus duplicate or inflate any measures derived from classroom_base.capacity. | when composing metrics like total_capacity_per_building: aggregate classroom_base (e.g., SUM(capacity) GROUP BY building) before joining to other one-row-per-building tables, or join to building-level tables only after aggregation to avoid duplication. | when composing averages or rates that use capacity as a denominator, ensure capacities are aggregated at the intended grain (e.g., average_capacity_per_building = AVG(capacity) GROUP BY building) before merging with datasets at a coarser grain.

views.description: Provides one row per physical classroom (building + room_number) with its seating capacity.

views.name: classroom_locations_distinct
views.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  classroom_base.building AS building,
  classroom_base.room_number AS room_number
FROM classroom_base

params.description: A deduplicated list of classroom locations (one row per unique building + room_number).
params.when_to_use: List all distinct classroom locations available in the data. | Filter or join other queries to only existing building + room_number combinations. | As a dimension-like input when you need unique classrooms to aggregate metrics (e.g., counts of events per room) — use as the grouping seed. | De-duplicate classroom references before joining to avoid multiplicative duplication when the source classroom_base contains repeated rows for the same room.
params.output_schema: building: classroom_base.building — building identifier/name taken directly from classroom_base. | room_number: classroom_base.room_number — room number taken directly from classroom_base.
params.metric: No derived numeric metrics in this view; outputs are raw distinct columns. If you need a count of distinct rooms, compute COUNT(*) or COUNT(*) OVER(...) after selecting from this view.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or lookup tables that are one-row-per-building or one-row-per-(building,room_number) on the exact keys — e.g., join to a building metadata view on building = classroom_locations_distinct.building — safe because classroom_locations_distinct is one-row-per-(building,room_number) so its rows (and any aggregated measures computed at that grain) will not be duplicated. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many fact tables (for example, an events or schedules table with many events per room) without re-aggregation on the fact table first, because joining this distinct-room view to a multi-row-per-room table will multiply rows and thus multiply any measures derived at the classroom_locations_distinct grain. | If you need to combine measures from a many-side table, aggregate that table to the (building, room_number) grain first (e.g., SELECT building, room_number, SUM(metric) AS metric_sum FROM fact_table GROUP BY building, room_number) and then join on (building, room_number). This preserves cardinality and ensures measures are not duplicated. | When composing into larger queries, treat this view as a dimension table at grain = (building, room_number). Any joins that preserve or reduce cardinality to that grain are safe; any joins that expand cardinality beyond that grain require re-aggregation of the expanding side.

views.name: classroom_by_capacity_cohort
views.body_sql:

FROM classroom_base c

params.description: Provides the seating capacity for each classroom (one row per building + room_number). Useful for queries that count classrooms per building or compute building-level average/aggregated capacities.
params.when_to_use: Count number of distinct classrooms per building (e.g., GROUP BY building to get classroom counts), excluding or filtering specific buildings. | Compute building-level average classroom capacity or other aggregates (e.g., AVG(capacity) GROUP BY building) for departments or building groups. | Filter classrooms by capacity ranges within a single building (e.g., classify rooms as 'Large/Medium/Small' and count those meeting a capacity threshold) and then aggregate counts.
params.output_schema: building: building identifier for the classroom (source: classroom_base.building) | room_number: room identifier within the building (source: classroom_base.room_number) | capacity: seating capacity of the room (source: classroom_base.capacity)
params.metric: capacity = classroom_base.capacity
params.composition: Cardinality-safe: join on (building, room_number) to other dimension tables that are one-row-per-(building,room_number) to preserve one-row-per-room semantics. | Cardinality-safe: join on building to tables that are one-row-per-building (e.g., a building dimension) — joining will not multiply room rows beyond the view's rows. | Not-safe without care: do not join directly to one-to-many fact tables (schedules, enrollments, events) on (building, room_number) if you intend to treat capacity as a room-level attribute in aggregated results. Either aggregate the fact table to (building, room_number) first, or join and then explicitly re-aggregate capacity (e.g., MAX(classroom_by_capacity_cohort.capacity)) to avoid duplicating room capacities.

Joining this one-row-per-room view directly to one-to-many fact tables will duplicate the capacity value unless the fact table is aggregated first or capacity is re-aggregated explicitly. | Do not rely on this view if you need columns not selected here (for example, any classroom attributes beyond building, room_number, capacity) — the view selects only those three columns from classroom_base.

views.name: building_classroom_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  COUNT(*) AS classroom_count,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number
FROM classroom
GROUP BY classroom.building

params.description: Per-building counts of classroom records (number of classroom rows per building) plus the room_number field included from the aggregated rows' grouping context.
params.when_to_use: Get total number of classrooms in each building | Report or filter by building-level classroom counts | Compose building-level aggregates into higher-level reports (e.g., campus summaries) without recounting classrooms | Join building-level classroom counts to dimension tables keyed by building
params.output_schema: building: identifier/name of the building — derived from classroom.building (grouped column) | classroom_count: count of classroom rows for that building — derived from COUNT(*) over classroom rows aggregated by classroom.building | room_number: a room_number value from the classroom rows — derived from classroom.room_number (note: room_number is not aggregated and is not functionally determined by building in the SQL; see composition guidance)
params.metric: classroom_count = COUNT(*) over rows grouped by classroom.building
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-building dimension (for example, a building_master or building_dimension view) on building — safe because building_classroom_counts is one-row-per-building and such a join is one-to-one, so classroom_count will not be duplicated | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: aggregate-then-join pattern: if joining to a child table that is one-to-many to building (for example, a table of events, maintenance records, or persons located in a building), first aggregate that child table to one-row-per-building (e.g., COUNT(event_id) GROUP BY building) and then join on building — safe because both sides are one-row-per-building when joined | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views keyed by building (for example, classroom_base if it is one row per classroom, or any view that lists individual rooms or events per room) without re-aggregation, because joining building_classroom_counts (one row per building) to a many-rows-per-building table will multiply rows and therefore inflate classroom_count | do NOT assume room_number is a deterministic attribute of building. The source SQL includes classroom.room_number in the select but groups only by classroom.building; SQL shown is invalid in strict SQL modes unless room_number is functionally dependent on building. Treat room_number as not reliably representing a single canonical room per building. If you need room_number reliably, use classroom_base or classroom_locations_distinct (which expose room-level detail) and then aggregate; avoid using room_number from this view for deterministic per-building logic | safe composition example: to get campus-level total classrooms, SUM(classroom_count) after joining building dimension or directly aggregate this view: SELECT SUM(classroom_count) FROM building_classroom_counts — safe because classroom_count is already per-building | unsafe composition example: SELECT bc.building, bc.classroom_count, COUNT(p.person_id) FROM building_classroom_counts bc JOIN person p ON p.building = bc.building GROUP BY bc.building — this will multiply bc.classroom_count unless you pre-aggregate person by building

views.description: Per-building counts of classroom records (number of classroom rows per building) plus the room_number field included from the aggregated rows' grouping context.

SELECT
  dept_name,

FROM department

params.description: Provides one-row-per-department basic attributes (dept_name, building, budget) for questions about department identity, location, and departmental budget-level aggregates.
params.when_to_use: Return department attributes (dept_name, building, budget) for display or reporting (e.g., list department names and buildings). | Compute department-level aggregates that use department budget as a measure (e.g., average or total budget per dept) when joined to already-aggregated results or when department is the intended grain. | Filter or group results by department (dept_name) when department is the desired grain (one row per dept_name).
params.output_schema: dept_name: department.dept_name — department name, one row per department | building: department.building — building associated with the department | budget: department.budget — numeric budget allocated to the department
params.metric: budget = department.budget
params.composition: This view is one-row-per-dept_name (department is the grain). It is safe to join to other one-row-per-department or aggregated-per-department/ per-building results without causing duplication. | Do NOT join department_base directly to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., students, sections, classrooms at their native grain) without re-aggregating the many side to dept_name first, because that will multiply department rows and duplicate budget. | When joining on building to building-level aggregates, ensure the other side is one-row-per-building (AGG) or that the relationship between department.building and that aggregate is intended; prefer joining to pre-aggregated building_classroom_counts (one row per building) rather than raw classroom rows. | If you need department-level budget combined with counts from another table, aggregate the other table to dept_name (e.g., SELECT dept_name, COUNT(*) ...) and then JOIN on dept_name to preserve department granularity.

views.name: department_budget_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  AVG(department.budget) AS avg_budget,
  COUNT(department.dept_name) AS dept_count,
  MIN(department.budget) AS min_budget,
  MAX(department.budget) AS max_budget
FROM department

params.description: Aggregated departmental budget statistics (average, count, min, max) across all departments.
params.when_to_use: Report total department-level budget summary (overall average, min, max, and number of departments). | Compare department budget aggregates across other dimensions after safe join/aggregation (e.g., by building or campus) when re-aggregated appropriately. | Serve as a pre-aggregated source for dashboards that need overall department budget metrics without scanning the department table again.
params.output_schema: avg_budget: the average of department.budget across all rows in the department table; derived from department.budget via AVG(department.budget). | dept_count: the count of department.dept_name values (number of department rows with non-NULL dept_name); derived from department.dept_name via COUNT(department.dept_name). | min_budget: the minimum value of department.budget across all department rows; derived from department.budget via MIN(department.budget). | max_budget: the maximum value of department.budget across all department rows; derived from department.budget via MAX(department.budget).
params.metric: avg_budget = AVG(department.budget) | dept_count = COUNT(department.dept_name) | min_budget = MIN(department.budget) | max_budget = MAX(department.budget)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional tables or views that are 1:1 or many-to-1 with the aggregated grain (here the view is at the entire-dataset/global grain — one row overall). Since this view returns a single row representing global aggregates, joining it directly to any other table without precautions will broadcast the single-row aggregates to every row of the other table but will not duplicate the aggregated measures. Example safe join: cross-join or attach to a report header or a one-row metadata table (no duplication issue because the stats are global). | do NOT join this aggregated view to a one-to-many detail table (e.g., employees, sections, classrooms) expecting the detail-level counts to remain intact unless you re-aggregate after the join. Although joining this single-row AGG to many-row tables does not multiply the AGG values (they are repeated), combining then aggregating without care can produce misleading results: if you need department-level aggregation by some dimension (e.g., per-building), compute department-level aggregates grouped by that key (a different AGG view) or join department (base) to the dimension and re-aggregate rather than joining this global AGG. | to obtain per-department metrics (grain = department), do not use this global view; instead use department_base (or a new aggregation grouped by department.dept_name) and then join to other 1:1 dimension tables on department.dept_name — safe because department-level aggregates are one-row-per-department. | Examples of safe compositions: join department_budget_stats into a dashboard alongside building_classroom_counts (AGG) as separate tiles (no join), or attach the single-row stats to a report via cross join or UI-level merge. Examples of unsafe compositions: joining department_budget_stats to section_room_assignment (JOIN) or classroom_base (NORM) and then aggregating expecting per-department correctness — those are one-to-many relationships relative to department rows and require re-aggregation at the desired grain first.

views.description: Aggregated departmental budget statistics (average, count, min, max) across all departments.

views.name: instructors_by_dept
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  instructor.ID AS ID,
  instructor.name AS name,
  instructor.dept_name AS dept_name,
  instructor.salary AS salary
FROM instructor

params.description: Provides one-row-per-instructor details (ID, name, department, salary) for questions about instructors and for composing instructor-level analyses.
params.when_to_use: Get instructor attributes (name, department, salary) for a specific instructor ID or list of IDs. | Filter or select instructors by department or salary thresholds. | Join instructor attributes onto other datasets at the instructor grain (e.g., sections taught, room assignments) to produce instructor-level reports. | Use as the base to aggregate instructor-level metrics (counts, average salary) or to build cohorted instructor summaries.
params.output_schema: ID: unique identifier for an instructor — derived from instructor.ID | name: instructor's name — derived from instructor.name | dept_name: name/key of the department the instructor belongs to — derived from instructor.dept_name | salary: instructor's salary (numeric) — derived from instructor.salary
params.metric: ID = instructor.ID | name = instructor.name | dept_name = instructor.dept_name | salary = instructor.salary
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base on department_base.dept_name = instructors_by_dept.dept_name — safe because department_base is one-row-per-department (dimension) and joining a one-row-per-instructor view to a department dimension will not multiply instructor rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to departments_rowlevel on departments_rowlevel.dept_name = instructors_by_dept.dept_name — safe if departments_rowlevel is one-row-per-department; this preserves the one-row-per-instructor grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom_locations_distinct on classroom_locations_distinct.building = <use only if you have instructor->building key available externally> — only safe when there is an explicit one-to-one relation enforced; instructors_by_dept itself does not contain building, so avoid relying on implicit duplication. | do NOT join directly to section_room_assignment (a JOIN view likely representing a many-to-many or one-to-many relationship between sections and rooms) without re-aggregating or first grouping section_room_assignment to instructor.ID (or another instructor-level key). Joining many sections per instructor directly will duplicate instructor rows and multiply salary or any instructor-level measures. | do NOT join directly to building_classroom_counts, classroom_by_capacity_cohort, or classroom_base if those views are at a classroom or building grain that can be many rows per instructor unless you aggregate those classroom-level rows to the instructor grain first (e.g., count of classrooms per instructor or avg classroom capacity per instructor). | When composing metrics: if you need instructor-level aggregates (for example total_sections_taught_by_instructor), compute those aggregates from a many-row sibling (sections or assignments) grouped by instructor.ID, then join the aggregated result to instructors_by_dept on ID. This prevents duplication of instructor-level measures (salary, counts) and keeps cardinality correct. | Planner hint: treat instructors_by_dept as strictly one-row-per-instructor. Any join to a table/view with potentially multiple rows per instructor must be preceded by grouping/aggregation to instructor.ID (or by using DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER filtering) so the instructor grain is preserved.

views.name: dept_top_instructor_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.dept_name AS dept_name,
  i.ID AS ID,
  i.name AS name,
  i.salary AS salary,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY i.dept_name ORDER BY i.salary DESC) AS salary_rank_in_dept
FROM instructor i

params.description: Ranks instructors by salary within their department and exposes instructor identity and salary at the instructor (ID) grain.
params.when_to_use: Find the top-paid instructors within each department (e.g., salary_rank_in_dept = 1). | Filter or list instructors by their salary rank inside their department (top N per department). | Compose further aggregations or joins that need one-row-per-instructor with an attached within-department salary rank.
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name for the instructor — derived from instructor.dept_name | ID: unique instructor identifier (the row grain) — derived from instructor.ID | name: instructor's name — derived from instructor.name | salary: instructor's salary (numeric) — derived from instructor.salary | salary_rank_in_dept: integer rank of the instructor's salary within their dept, 1 = highest salary — derived from RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY instructor.dept_name ORDER BY instructor.salary DESC)
params.metric: salary_rank_in_dept = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY instructor.dept_name ORDER BY instructor.salary DESC)  -- a window ranking per dept; NOT an aggregate across rows | salary = instructor.salary  -- base numeric measure at instructor grain
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base (or departments_rowlevel) on dept_name = dept_name — safe because department_base is one-row-per-department, so joining preserves this view's one-row-per-instructor grain and does NOT duplicate instructor rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to instructors_by_dept (SEL sibling) only if it is also one-row-per-instructor (verify schema) — safe when it is 1:1 with instructor.ID; otherwise treat as many-to-one or aggregate before joining. | do NOT join directly to section_room_assignment or any section-level or classroom-level table/view (one-to-many from instructor) without first aggregating those tables to instructor-level (e.g., count of sections per instructor) — such joins would multiply instructor rows and therefore duplicate salary and rank measures unless you re-aggregate after the join. | do NOT join to building_classroom_counts, classroom_by_capacity_cohort, classroom_locations_distinct, or other classroom/section AGG/JOIN views that are many-to-many relative to instructor without an explicit aggregation keyed to instructor.ID — those will multiply this view's instructor rows if the join key is not strictly one-to-one. | When composing aggregates on top of this view (for example: count of top-ranked instructors per department), aggregate at the appropriate key (e.g., dept_name) rather than relying on this view's salary_rank_in_dept as an aggregate; salary_rank_in_dept is a windowed ordinal and must be re-evaluated or used as a filter prior to aggregation. | If you need measures that remain correct after joining to many-child tables, either: (a) pre-aggregate the child table to instructor.ID (one row per instructor) and then join, or (b) join and then GROUP BY the instructor-level columns from this view and re-compute aggregates (e.g., MAX(salary), MIN(salary), COUNT(DISTINCT instructor.ID)).

views.name: classroom_capacity_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  AVG(classroom.capacity) AS avg_capacity,
  COUNT(classroom.room_number) AS classroom_count,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number
FROM classroom
GROUP BY classroom.building

params.description: Provides per-building classroom capacity summary: average classroom capacity and count of distinct classrooms in each building.
params.when_to_use: Report average classroom size by building | Rank or filter buildings by typical classroom capacity | Compose building-level capacity metrics into larger reports (e.g., compare capacity to departmental metrics) as a building-grain source | Drive dashboards or alerts that need number of classrooms and mean capacity per building
params.output_schema: building: building identifier/name from classroom.building (the grouping key) | avg_capacity: average of classroom.capacity over all classroom rows per building (derived from AVG(classroom.capacity)) | classroom_count: count of classroom.room_number rows per building (derived from COUNT(classroom.room_number))
params.metric: avg_capacity = AVG(classroom.capacity) — average capacity of classrooms within the building; computed at the building grain | classroom_count = COUNT(classroom.room_number) — number of classroom rows (rooms) present for the building as found in the classroom table; computed at the building grain
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to building_classroom_counts on building — safe because this view is one-row-per-building (the same grain), so joining on building will not duplicate measures when both sides are aggregated at building level | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom_locations_distinct on building — safe when classroom_locations_distinct is also one-row-per-building (or otherwise deduplicated to building) because this view is one-row-per-building | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base or departments_rowlevel on building only if those views are one-row-per-building; otherwise re-aggregate after join. Only join without re-aggregation when the other side is also at building grain | do NOT join directly to section_room_assignment (one-to-many from classroom/building to section assignments) without re-aggregating the multiplied rows first, because joining to a one-to-many table will duplicate avg_capacity and classroom_count measures and inflate them unless you re-aggregate back to building grain after the join | do NOT join directly to classroom_base or instructors_by_dept (if they are row-level or one-to-many) without aggregating those tables to building grain first; otherwise measures in this view will be multiplied by the number of matching detail rows | When composing: if you need building-level metrics combined with lower-grain details (e.g., section counts per building), either (a) aggregate the lower-grain data to building before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate using appropriate aggregate functions (e.g., SUM, AVG over weighted counts) to restore building grain. This ensures avg_capacity and classroom_count remain correct and not duplicated.

views.description: Provides per-building classroom capacity summary: average classroom capacity and count of distinct classrooms in each building.

views.name: department_budget_by_building_join

SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.building AS "department.building",
  d.budget AS budget,
  c.avg_capacity AS avg_capacity,
  c.classroom_count AS classroom_count
FROM department AS d
LEFT JOIN classroom_capacity_by_building AS c

params.description: Provides department-level budget and associated building-level classroom capacity metrics by department name.

params.composition: Safe to join to department_base (or departments_rowlevel) on department.dept_name — safe because this view is one row per dept_name (grain = dept_name); joining to additional one-row-per-department tables does not duplicate measures. | Safe to join to building_classroom_counts or classroom_capacity_by_building on building — safe only if the target view/table is one-row-per-building (these are building-level aggregates); joins will not multiply building-level measures when building is unique in the other side. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many detail tables such as classroom_base, section_room_assignment, or classroom_locations_distinct without first re-aggregating the detail to department (or building) grain — joining directly would duplicate department-level budget and the building-level measures because those detail tables have multiple rows per building or per department. | If you need to combine with instructor or section-level data (e.g., instructors_by_dept, section_room_assignment), either: (a) aggregate the detail side to dept_name (or building) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate, ensuring you SUM/AVERAGE budget/avg_capacity appropriately and avoid summing budget across duplicated department rows. | When computing derived metrics that divide budget by classroom counts (e.g., budget_per_classroom = budget / classroom_count), it is safe to compute directly from this view because classroom_count is already a building-level aggregate aligned by department.building; ensure classroom_count is not zero (handle nulls) before dividing. | If you need a strict building-grain result, prefer using classroom_capacity_by_building directly; this view repeats building-level metrics per department where multiple departments share the same building.

views.name: classroom_base_12

SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,

FROM classroom

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like, one-row-per-building views such as classroom_capacity_by_building(AGG) or building-level views on building = classroom.building — safe because classroom_base_12 is one row per (building, room_number) and those building-level views are aggregated per building, so measures are not duplicated when joining on building (you will get the classroom-level rows each augmented with building aggregates). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base(NORM) or departments_rowlevel(SEL) only when there is a one-to-one or many-to-one relationship from classroom to department (e.g., if department is keyed by building and that relationship is one-to-one). Validate keys before joining; the view itself does not enforce department linkage. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail/join views like section_room_assignment(JOIN) or department_budget_by_building_join(JOIN) without re-aggregating the detail first, because those views can have multiple rows per (building, room_number) or per building which would multiply classroom_base_12 rows and thus duplicate capacity values. If you need combined metrics (for example, total scheduled seats), first aggregate the many-side (e.g., COUNT or SUM by building,room_number) then join to this view. | If composing higher-level aggregates from classroom_base_12 (for example SUM(capacity) by building), perform the aggregation on this view itself rather than relying on joins to other non-aggregated detail tables; that preserves correct cardinality. | Safe composition example: SELECT bldg, SUM(capacity) FROM classroom_base_12 GROUP BY bldg — produces total capacity per building without duplication. | Unsafe composition example: SELECT c.building, c.room_number, c.capacity, s.section_id FROM classroom_base_12 c JOIN section_room_assignment s ON s.building = c.building AND s.room_number = c.room_number — this will replicate c.capacity for each matching section row; to avoid duplication, aggregate section_room_assignment first (e.g., COUNT(sections) per classroom) or deduplicate sections before joining.

views.name: classroom_capacity_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,
  classroom.capacity AS capacity
FROM classroom

params.description: Provides the capacity (seating) for each classroom identified by building and room_number.
params.when_to_use: Look up the capacity for a specific classroom (by building + room_number). | Compose queries that need classroom capacity as a per-room attribute (e.g., capacity joins to sections or scheduling). | Build aggregates of capacity across rooms after joining or grouping (e.g., total capacity per building or cohorting by capacity ranges).
params.output_schema: building: building identifier for the classroom — derived from classroom.building | room_number: room identifier within the building — derived from classroom.room_number | capacity: seating capacity (numeric) of the classroom — derived from classroom.capacity

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom_base (NORM) on (building, room_number) — safe because classroom_capacity_cohort is one-row-per-(building,room_number) and classroom_base should also be one-row-per-(building,room_number), so measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom_locations_distinct (SEL) on (building, room_number) — safe when that view is one-row-per-(building,room_number); this preserves one-row-per-room semantics and does not multiply capacity. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom_capacity_by_building (AGG) on building — safe only if you aggregate classroom_capacity_cohort appropriately first (e.g., SUM(capacity) GROUP BY building) or if classroom_capacity_by_building is a pre-aggregated metric per building; joining the raw per-room rows to a per-building aggregate is safe because the aggregate is one-row-per-building and will not duplicate the per-building aggregate when joined to a single per-building row, but be mindful that joining a building-level aggregate back to multiple room rows will repeat the same aggregate value for each room row — this is usually acceptable but consider whether you want repeated values or a separate query. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to section_room_assignment (JOIN) on (building, room_number) if section_room_assignment is one-to-many (multiple sections assigned to the same room) when your intent is to preserve per-room measures: joining will multiply classroom_capacity_cohort rows by the number of matching sections and thus duplicate capacity values. Instead, either (a) aggregate the joined results (e.g., compute AVG or MAX capacity per section grouping) or (b) first aggregate section_room_assignment to one row per (building, room_number) before joining. | do NOT join without care to building_classroom_counts (AGG) on building if that aggregate is one-row-per-building: joining will attach the per-building counts to each room row (repeating the same count for every room) — this is safe if repetition is intended, but unsafe if the planner expects measures to remain at room grain; to combine measures at different grains, explicitly aggregate classroom_capacity_cohort to building grain (e.g., SUM(capacity) GROUP BY building) before joining. | safe composition pattern: when building higher-level metrics (e.g., total capacity per building), perform aggregation on classroom_capacity_cohort (SUM(capacity) GROUP BY building) and then join to building-level views/aggregates on building — this prevents accidental duplication. | general rule: classroom_capacity_cohort is strictly at the grain (building, room_number). Any join to a one-to-many relation keyed by (building, room_number) will multiply rows and thus duplicate the capacity value; such joins require pre-aggregation or distincting of the many-side to remain cardinality-safe.

views.description: Provides the capacity (seating) for each classroom identified by building and room_number.

views.name: department_with_courses_count
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  COUNT(c.course_id) AS course_count
FROM
  department d
LEFT JOIN
  course c
ON
  d.dept_name = c.dept_name
GROUP BY
  d.dept_name

params.description: Provides the number of courses offered per department (one row per department with its course count).
params.when_to_use: Report or dashboard showing how many courses exist in each department | Filter or rank departments by course count (e.g., top-N departments by number of courses) | As an aggregated building block when joining department-level metrics to other department-level datasets | Compose with other department-level aggregates (budgets, instructors) without re-aggregation
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (sourced from department.dept_name) | course_count: count of courses associated with the department (derived from COUNT(course.course_id))
params.metric: course_count = COUNT(course.course_id)  -- aggregated measure computed by counting course.course_id for rows with the same department.dept_name (LEFT JOIN ensures departments with zero courses appear with count 0 in SQL semantics that coerce NULL to 0; note: some SQL engines may return 0 vs NULL differently so treat as aggregated count)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base (or any other one-row-per-department view/table) on department.dept_name — safe because department_with_courses_count has exactly one row per dept_name, so joining on dept_name to another one-row-per-department dataset will not duplicate course_count. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_budget_stats (AGG) on dept_name — safe because both sides are aggregated to department level (one row per dept_name) so measures remain aligned and not multiplied. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to departments_rowlevel (SEL) on dept_name only if departments_rowlevel is also one-row-per-department; verify cardinality first. If departments_rowlevel is multi-row per department, aggregate it to department level before joining. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as course (base table), section_room_assignment (JOIN), classroom_base, instructors_by_dept (if that view is multi-row per dept) or any view that contains multiple rows per dept without first aggregating them to department level — doing so will multiply course_count because department_with_courses_count is one row per dept and joining a multi-row child will replicate that row for each child row. | If you need department_with_courses_count together with a child-level detail (e.g., list of courses, sections), either (a) join the child table to department_base and recompute COUNT(...) grouped by department, or (b) join department_with_courses_count to a derived aggregated child result (one row per dept) so that measures remain correct. | When composing further metrics that sum course_count across departments, sums are safe because course_count is additive at the department grain. Avoid merging at a finer grain (e.g., building or classroom) without mapping departments to that finer grain via a deterministic one-to-one or aggregated relationship.

views.description: Provides the number of courses offered per department (one row per department with its course count).

views.name: department_with_instructors_and_students
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.building AS building,
  COALESCE(i.instructor_count, 0) AS instructor_count,
  COALESCE(s.student_count, 0) AS student_count
FROM department d
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT dept_name, COUNT(*) AS instructor_count
  FROM instructor
  GROUP BY dept_name
) i ON i.dept_name = d.dept_name
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT dept_name, COUNT(*) AS student_count
  FROM student
  GROUP BY dept_name
) s ON s.dept_name = d.dept_name

params.description: Per-department summary listing department name, building, and counts of instructors and students in that department.
params.when_to_use: Show a department-level roster or matrix with counts of instructors and students per department | Filter or display departments with zero or more instructors/students (includes departments with no instructors or no students) | Serve as the starting aggregated input when composing higher-level dashboards or reports that need department-level headcounts alongside department attributes
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (derived from department.dept_name) | building: department building/location (derived from department.building) | instructor_count: number of instructor rows assigned to this department (derived from COUNT(*) over instructor grouped by instructor.dept_name) | student_count: number of student rows assigned to this department (derived from COUNT(*) over student grouped by student.dept_name)
params.metric: instructor_count = COUNT(*) of instructor rows grouped by instructor.dept_name (implemented in the view's subquery and COALESCE to 0 when no match) | student_count = COUNT(*) of student rows grouped by student.dept_name (implemented in the view's subquery and COALESCE to 0 when no match)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base on department.dept_name = department_base.dept_name — safe because this view is one row per dept_name (the grain), so joining another one-row-per-department dimension will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to departments_rowlevel (or any other department-level 1:1 view) on dept_name — safe because both sides are at the same department grain. | do NOT join directly to instructor (or any table/view that is one-to-many from department to instructor) without first aggregating that instructor data to department grain (e.g., instructors_by_dept) — otherwise instructor_count will be multiplied and become incorrect. | do NOT join directly to student (or any table/view that is one-to-many from department to student) without first aggregating student data to department grain (e.g., a students_by_dept aggregate) — otherwise student_count will be multiplied and become incorrect. | safe composition pattern: if you need to combine this view with other aggregated measures from one-to-many children (e.g., section counts, classroom counts), pre-aggregate those children to dept_name and then join on dept_name so all measures remain at the same department grain. | example safe join: JOIN building_classroom_counts ON department_with_instructors_and_students.building = building_classroom_counts.building — safe only if building_classroom_counts is one-row-per-building; this join will not duplicate department-level counts as long as building_classroom_counts is unique on building. | when joining to views with different grain, either (a) aggregate the other view up to dept_name, or (b) re-aggregate after the join and compute measures from base tables again. Do not rely on this view's instructor_count or student_count if you perform a join that can multiply department rows.

views.description: Per-department summary listing department name, building, and counts of instructors and students in that department.

views.name: department_budget_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.building AS building,
  d.budget AS budget,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY d.budget DESC) AS budget_rank
FROM department AS d

params.description: Provides each department's name, building, budget, and the department budget rank (dense, highest budget = rank 1).
params.when_to_use: Ask for departments ordered or compared by budget (e.g., which departments have the top budgets). | Compose dashboards or reports that show department-level budget and relative standing among departments. | Join department-level contextual attributes (building) to other department-level metrics without duplicating budget measures. | Filter or aggregate departments by budget rank (e.g., show departments with budget_rank <= N).
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name (derived from department.dept_name) | building: building associated with the department (derived from department.building) | budget: department budget numeric value (derived from department.budget) | budget_rank: dense rank of department budget in descending order (derived from DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY department.budget DESC))
params.metric: budget = department.budget | budget_rank = DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY department.budget DESC)  -- a window ranking over all department rows; dense ranking gives consecutive ranks for equal budgets
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base (or any view that is one-row-per-department) on department.dept_name — safe because department_budget_rank is one-row-per-dept_name, so measures (budget, budget_rank) are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dept_top_instructor_rank (RANK) on dept_name — safe if the sibling view is also one-row-per-department; confirm sibling view's grain is dept_name before joining. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as instructors_by_dept (if it is one row per instructor) or section_room_assignment (many sections) without re-aggregating the one-to-many side to department-level first, because joining those would multiply rows and thus duplicate budget and corrupt budget_rank semantics. | When joining to building-level aggregates (e.g., classroom_capacity_by_building or building_classroom_counts), join on building = building — this is safe only if those building-level views are one-row-per-building. If they are one-to-many to building, re-aggregate to building-level before joining. | If you need department-level aggregations after joining to one-to-many detail (for example, total instructor salary per department), perform the aggregation on the joined result grouped by dept_name to restore one-row-per-department and then recompute or preserve budget_rank as appropriate (note: recomputing rank over a grouped result will change ranks if departments are filtered). | Avoid joining to sibling JOIN views that expand department rows into multiple rows per dept (e.g., department_budget_by_building_join) unless you explicitly want a multi-row-per-department result — in that case budget and budget_rank are repeated per output row and should be handled accordingly (e.g., aggregate budget using MAX or SUM depending on intended semantics).

views.description: Provides each department's name, building, budget, and the department budget rank (dense, highest budget = rank 1).

views.name: department_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.building AS building,
  COUNT(d.dept_name) AS dept_count,
  MAX(d.budget) AS max_budget,
  MIN(d.budget) AS min_budget,
  AVG(d.budget) AS avg_budget
FROM department d
GROUP BY d.building

params.description: Per-building aggregates of how many departments are located there and summary statistics (max, min, average) of their budgets.
params.when_to_use: Report the number of departments and budget summaries for each building (one row per building). | Filter or rank buildings by department count or budget statistics. | Compose higher-level metrics that need department-level budget summaries per building (e.g., combine with building capacity or classroom counts) while preserving correct aggregation semantics.
params.output_schema: building: building identifier / name from department.building (GROUP BY key). | dept_count: count of departments in the building, derived from COUNT(department.dept_name). | max_budget: maximum department.budget among departments in the building, derived from MAX(department.budget). | min_budget: minimum department.budget among departments in the building, derived from MIN(department.budget). | avg_budget: average department.budget among departments in the building, derived from AVG(department.budget).
params.metric: dept_count = COUNT(department.dept_name)  -- integer count of department rows per building | max_budget = MAX(department.budget)       -- numeric maximum budget per building | min_budget = MIN(department.budget)       -- numeric minimum budget per building | avg_budget = AVG(department.budget)       -- numeric average budget per building
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension or lookup that is one-row-per-building (for example a building_base or building lookup view) on department_by_building.building = building_base.building — safe because department_by_building is already one-row-per-building so its measures will not be duplicated. | Safe to join to building_classroom_counts (AGG) on building — both are one-row-per-building aggregate views; joining them preserves the one-row-per-building cardinality and does not multiply measures. | Do NOT join department_by_building directly to one-to-many tables/views keyed by building (for example department_base if it contains one row per department, classroom tables with multiple classrooms per building, section_room_assignment if it assigns many sections to rooms in the same building, or instructors_by_dept if it is one-to-many to departments) without re-aggregating the one-to-many side first. Directly joining to such one-to-many tables will multiply dept_count, max_budget, min_budget, and avg_budget rows and therefore distort the aggregates. | If you must combine with a one-to-many relationship (e.g., classrooms, sections, or instructors), either: (a) aggregate the one-to-many side to one-row-per-building before joining, or (b) join first and then re-aggregate using appropriate aggregates (e.g., SUM of dept_count after grouping by building if dept_count is to be additive, or recompute max/min/avg from raw budget values). | When composing additional aggregated metrics from department_by_building, treat dept_count as a pre-aggregated metric (count per building). Avoid summing avg_budget across buildings to compute an overall average; instead, if an overall average budget across departments is required, recompute AVG on department.budget at the appropriate grain or carry department-level counts+sum to compute weighted averages: SUM(dept_count * avg_budget) / SUM(dept_count) if building-level weighted average is acceptable and dept_count represents department counts used as weights.

views.description: Per-building aggregates of how many departments are located there and summary statistics (max, min, average) of their budgets.

views.name: classroom_by_building_agg

SELECT

  COUNT(room_number) AS classroom_count,

params.description: Aggregated classroom counts and average seating capacity per building.
params.when_to_use: Get the number of classrooms and average capacity for each building (building-level summaries). | Compose building-level reports that need classroom counts or average capacity as inputs. | Join to other building-level datasets (e.g., building budgets or building attributes) without re-aggregation. | Filter or rank buildings by classroom_count or avg_capacity.
params.output_schema: building: building identifier string or code as provided by classroom.building (grouping key). | classroom_count: number of classroom rows in the classroom table for the building; derived from COUNT(room_number) in the view SQL. | avg_capacity: average of the capacity column for classroom rows in the building; derived from AVG(capacity) in the view SQL.
params.metric: classroom_count = COUNT(classroom.room_number)  -- a COUNT aggregate over classroom rows per building | avg_capacity = AVG(classroom.capacity)  -- an AVG aggregate over classroom.capacity per building
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to building-level views/tables (one-row-per-building) such as building_classroom_counts (AGG) or department_budget_by_building_join on building — safe because classroom_by_building_agg is one-row-per-building and joining to another one-row-per-building relation will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to building dimension tables (e.g., a buildings table keyed by building) on classroom_by_building_agg.building = buildings.building — safe because the buildings table should be one-row-per-building and will not duplicate aggregates. | UNSAFE to join directly to one-to-many detail tables or views (e.g., section_room_assignment, instructors_by_dept if linked many-to-one through building, or classroom rows themselves) without re-aggregation. Joining classroom_by_building_agg to a child table that has multiple rows per building will multiply classroom_count and avg_capacity values and produce incorrect totals. | If you must combine with a one-to-many relation (for example, section_room_assignment or departments_rowlevel if multiple rows per building), either: (a) re-aggregate after the join (e.g., SUM(classroom_count) with appropriate GROUP BY), or (b) join the child relation to the underlying classroom table first and compute needed metrics at the final desired grain. Do not assume classroom_by_building_agg's aggregates remain correct through such joins. | When composing further aggregations, treat classroom_count as an additive metric (it can be summed across disjoint building groups). Do not sum avg_capacity directly across buildings to get a correct overall average; instead compute a weighted average using SUM(classroom_count * avg_capacity) / SUM(classroom_count) or derive from underlying classroom.capacity if available. | Joins to sibling aggregate views: joining two AGG views that share the same grain 'building' is safe (one-row-per-building). Example safe join: classroom_by_building_agg JOIN classroom_capacity_by_building ON building. | Do NOT join to views that are known to be at a lower grain (many rows per building) such as section_room_assignment(JOIN) without first aggregating that relation to one row per building; otherwise classroom_count and avg_capacity will be duplicated.

views.name: classroom_size_buckets
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  building,
  room_number,
  capacity,
  CASE
    WHEN capacity IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN capacity <= pct_33 THEN 'small'
    WHEN capacity <= pct_66 THEN 'medium'
    ELSE 'large'
  END AS size_category
FROM (
  SELECT
    c.building,
    c.room_number,
    c.capacity,
    -- compute empirical tercile cutpoints per available capacities
    (SELECT capacity FROM classroom_base cb WHERE cb.capacity IS NOT NULL ORDER BY capacity LIMIT 1 OFFSET ( (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM classroom_base cb2 WHERE cb2.capacity IS NOT NULL) / 3 ) ) AS pct_33,
    (SELECT capacity FROM classroom_base cb WHERE cb.capacity IS NOT NULL ORDER BY capacity LIMIT 1 OFFSET ( 2 * ( (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM classroom_base cb2 WHERE cb2.capacity IS NOT NULL) / 3 ) ) ) AS pct_66
  FROM classroom_base c
)

params.description: Categorizes classrooms (by building and room_number) into size buckets (small/medium/large) based on empirical tercile cutpoints of capacity.
params.when_to_use: Ask for the size category (small/medium/large) of each classroom identified by building and room_number. | Filter or group classrooms by size_category in downstream analyses (e.g., counts of rooms by size, join to schedules to find sections in large rooms). | Compose with other classroom-level data where a single row per classroom is required (e.g., join to classroom attributes or locations).
params.output_schema: building: building identifier for the classroom — derived directly from classroom_base.building | room_number: room identifier within the building — derived directly from classroom_base.room_number | capacity: seating capacity of the room — derived directly from classroom_base.capacity | size_category: bucket label ('small', 'medium', 'large', or NULL) computed from capacity relative to empirical tercile cutpoints (pct_33 and pct_66) computed from classroom_base.capacity
params.metric: capacity = classroom_base.capacity | size_category = CASE WHEN classroom_base.capacity IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN classroom_base.capacity <= pct_33 THEN 'small' WHEN classroom_base.capacity <= pct_66 THEN 'medium' ELSE 'large' END | pct_33 = (SELECT capacity FROM classroom_base cb WHERE cb.capacity IS NOT NULL ORDER BY capacity LIMIT 1 OFFSET ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM classroom_base cb2 WHERE cb2.capacity IS NOT NULL) / 3)) — empirical 33rd percentile cutpoint (tercile) computed via OFFSET | pct_66 = (SELECT capacity FROM classroom_base cb WHERE cb.capacity IS NOT NULL ORDER BY capacity LIMIT 1 OFFSET (2 * ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM classroom_base cb2 WHERE cb2.capacity IS NOT NULL) / 3))) — empirical 66th percentile cutpoint (tercile) computed via OFFSET
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE joins (do not duplicate rows/measures): join to table/view that is one-row-per-building-room_number, e.g., classroom_locations_distinct on (building, room_number) — safe because classroom_size_buckets is one row per (building, room_number), so measures (capacity, size_category) are not duplicated. | Safe to join to classroom_base on (building, room_number) — classroom_base is the base row-level table this view is derived from; join will be 1:1 for the same grain. | Safe to left-join to building-level aggregates that are one-row-per-building (e.g., classroom_capacity_by_building) on building if those aggregates are pre-aggregated to building — safe because the join is one-to-many only if you repeat classroom rows per building aggregate, but joining a one-row-per-building aggregate to one-row-per-room will expand rows from building to rooms in a controlled way (does not multiply room-level measures beyond their one row). | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views without re-aggregation first, for example do NOT join to section_room_assignment (likely multiple sections per room) on (building, room_number) without aggregating sections first — such a join would duplicate classroom_size_buckets rows for each matching section and thereby multiply counts/measures that assume one-row-per-classroom. | Do NOT join to building_classroom_counts or other AGG views that are at a different grain unless you understand and handle the grain change (either aggregate this view up to building first or join in a way that avoids duplicating classroom rows). | If you need section-level results combined with size_category, first aggregate or filter section_room_assignment to one row per (building, room_number) (for example, count sections per room) then join to this view on (building, room_number) — this preserves cardinality safety. | Planner guidance: this view's grain is building+room_number (one row per classroom). Treat capacity and size_category as row-level attributes, not as aggregations to be summed across joins unless you explicitly re-aggregate after any join that increases cardinality.

When joining to a one-row-per-building view, join on building and then you will not duplicate counts as long as you keep grouping at building (or re-aggregate appropriately). | Safe to join to higher-grain building metadata (e.g., department or budget summaries that are one-row-per-building) on building — the measures in this view will not be multiplied because those tables are one-to-one with building. | Do NOT join directly to any one-to-many table/view keyed by building (for example: section_room_assignment, classroom_locations_distinct if it contains multiple rows per classroom, instructors_by_dept if multiple instructors per building, or departments_rowlevel if many departments map to the same building) without re-aggregation. All output columns are direct projections (no aggregate expressions). | If you need a derived metric at the course grain, compute it outside this view, e.g. course_credit_count = SUM(credits) GROUP BY course_id (but credits is already at course grain so SUM is usually unnecessary).

params.description: Lists direct prerequisite relationships between courses (one row per course → prerequisite pair).
params.when_to_use: Find all direct prerequisites for a given course_id or set of course_ids. | Build course dependency graphs (one-hop edges) or count direct prerequisites per course when aggregated. | Filter or join prerequisite edges to course or department dimension tables before further aggregation.

views.name: prereq_counts_per_course

  p.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.prereq_id) AS distinct_prereq_count
FROM
  prereq p
GROUP BY
  p.course_id

params.description: Counts the number of distinct prerequisite courses for each course (one row per course_id).
params.when_to_use: Report or dashboard that needs the number of unique prerequisites per course (e.g., course complexity, prerequisite load). | Join into a course-level dataset to display or filter courses by how many distinct prerequisites they require. | Compose into higher-level aggregates (department or instructor level) by joining to course → department/instructor dimensions and re-aggregating.
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier for a course; derived from prereq.course_id | distinct_prereq_count: integer count of unique prerequisite course identifiers for the given course_id; derived from COUNT(DISTINCT prereq.prereq_id)
params.metric: distinct_prereq_count = COUNT(DISTINCT prereq.prereq_id) grouped by prereq.course_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a course or course-dimension view/table on course_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-course_id, so joining to a 1-to-1 or many-to-1 course dimension will not duplicate the distinct_prereq_count. | Safe join example: JOIN course_dim d ON prereq_counts_per_course.course_id = d.course_id — d is expected to be at most one row per course_id. | Safe composition for roll-up: to compute department-level total/average prerequisite counts, first join prereq_counts_per_course to a course→department mapping on course_id (one-row-per-course), then aggregate distinct_prereq_count at the department level (e.g., SUM or AVG). Re-aggregate after joining; do NOT sum across joins that introduce course duplication without re-aggregation. | do NOT join directly (without re-aggregation) to any table/view that is one-to-many from course_id to multiple rows (for example, a sections table, enrollments, or any assignment table keyed by course_id that has multiple rows per course). Such joins will duplicate the row for a course and thus multiply distinct_prereq_count. If you must join to a one-to-many relation, either: |   - pre-aggregate that relation to one row per course_id before joining, or |   - join and then re-aggregate the result grouping by the desired grain (e.g., course_id) to restore correct measures. | Examples of NOT safe (without re-aggregation): joining to section_room_assignment or any sections/enrollments table that has multiple rows per course_id, because those joins will replicate the course-level measure and inflate counts. | When composing into larger aggregates (department, building, instructor), treat distinct_prereq_count as a course-level metric and aggregate (SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX) after joining to a dimension that maps course_id to the higher-level key to avoid double-counting.

params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base (NORM) on department.dept_name — safe because this view is one-row-per-dept_name (its grain is dept_name), so joining on dept_name will not duplicate this view's rows or its budget values. | Safe to join to dept_top_instructor_rank (RANK) or instructors_by_dept (SEL) on dept_name only if those sibling views are one-row-per-department (confirm their grains). If they are one-row-per-dept_name, join will not duplicate; if they are one-to-many (multiple instructors per dept) you must aggregate those views to one row per dept before joining, otherwise budget will be multiplied. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables/views such as classroom_base (NORM), section_room_assignment (JOIN), building_classroom_counts (AGG) (if that AGG is per-building or per-classroom and not per-dept), or classroom_locations_distinct without ensuring the join key relationship is one-to-one. Joining departments_with_building to building-level aggregates (e.g., classroom_capacity_by_building) is safe if you accept that multiple department rows can match the same building aggregate (this does not duplicate budget within a single department row). However, if the intent is to preserve department budgets while rolling up to building totals, aggregate budgets by building before joining to building-level aggregates to avoid double-counting. | If composing aggregations that include budget (e.g., SUM(budget) partitioned by building), perform the aggregation on departments_with_building (GROUP BY building) rather than joining to a many-side table first. In other words: push aggregation of budget to this view's grain (dept_name) or to the desired grouping level before joining to many-side relations. | Summary rules: join one-row-per-department dimensions (or normalized department_base) on dept_name safely; when joining to many-side relations (classrooms, sections, instructors with multiple rows per dept), either (a) aggregate the many-side to the department grain or to the join key's grain first, or (b) aggregate budget after the join with DISTINCT or appropriate grouping to avoid multiplying budget measures.

params.description: Provides the set of prerequisite relationships between courses as pairs (course_id, prereq_id).
params.when_to_use: Find direct prerequisite courses for a given course | Build a prerequisite graph or path (one-hop edges) between courses | Filter or join course-level facts to include prerequisite relationships | Compose into queries that count prerequisites per course (must aggregate after joining if joining to many rows)

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a course-dimension or course-base view (e.g., any course_base or course-level view) on course_id or prereq_id — safe because prereq_edges is one-row-per (course_id, prereq_id) and joining to a one-row-per-course dimension on the matching key will not duplicate measures from that course dimension. | Safe: join to a course-level view on prereq.course_id = course_base.course_id (or prereq_id = course_base.course_id) because the course-level view is expected to be one row per course; this does not multiply rows from the course-level view. | Not safe without re-aggregation: do NOT join prereq_edges directly to one-to-many detail tables (for example, a enrollments or sections table that has multiple rows per course) when you intend to preserve counts or aggregated measures from prereq_edges, because those joins will multiply prereq_edges rows and thus duplicate any derived counts unless you re-aggregate after the join. | If you need counts of prerequisites per course combined with many-row fact tables, either (a) aggregate prereq_edges first to get one row per course (e.g., COUNT(prereq_id) GROUP BY course_id) then join, or (b) join and then use DISTINCT or appropriate GROUP BY to avoid double-counting. | When composing multi-hop prerequisite paths (e.g., course -> prereq -> prereq_of_prereq), you may self-join prereq_edges on prereq_id = course_id; this is safe because the intent is to expand edges and the result will correctly represent the expanded edge set (it will increase cardinality according to graph structure).

  p.course_id

params.description: Counts the number of distinct prerequisite courses for each course (one row per course_id).
params.when_to_use: Report: How many prerequisites does each course have? | Filter or rank courses by number of prerequisites (e.g., top courses with most prereqs). | Join with a course dimension to display course metadata alongside its prereq count. | Compose into higher-level aggregations (e.g., average number of prereqs by department) by joining to department or course tables and re-aggregating.
params.output_schema: course_id: identifier of the target course that has prerequisites. Derived from prereq.course_id. | num_prereqs: integer count of distinct prerequisite course identifiers for the given course_id. Derived from COUNT(DISTINCT prereq.prereq_id) in the prereq table.
params.metric: num_prereqs = COUNT(DISTINCT prereq.prereq_id)  -- aggregated per prereq.course_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a course dimension (e.g., course_base or another one-row-per-course view) on course_id — safe because course_prereq_counts is one-row-per-course_id and joining to a one-row-per-course dimension preserves that cardinality, so num_prereqs will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department or other higher-level one-row-per-course-id views on course_id, then re-aggregate as needed (for example, to compute average num_prereqs per department use: SELECT dept_id, AVG(num_prereqs) FROM course_prereq_counts JOIN course_dim USING(course_id) GROUP BY dept_id). This is safe because the join is to one-row-per-course and aggregation is performed afterward. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many child tables or views keyed by course_id (e.g., sections, enrollments, or any section-level view that has multiple rows per course) without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply rows for a given course_id and thus inflate num_prereqs. If you need to combine with a many-rows-per-course dataset, either: |   - aggregate the child dataset to one row per course_id before joining (e.g., COUNT(section_id) per course_id), or |   - join first and then compute aggregates from scratch using the underlying prereq table rather than relying on num_prereqs as a pre-aggregated measure. | When composing into joins that introduce additional grouping keys (for example, joining to a term or semester table through a many-to-many relation), ensure you re-aggregate num_prereqs appropriately (SUM is not appropriate to combine counts across courses unless the grouping key is at least course-level; typically use AVG, MIN, MAX, or recompute distinct counts from prereq when necessary). | Because num_prereqs uses COUNT(DISTINCT prereq_id), any composition that needs to preserve the distinctness of prereq_id across additional join paths should either: (a) re-run a DISTINCT count on the prereq table with the intended join filters, or (b) ensure the join path does not introduce duplicate prereq_id rows for a given course_id.

views.name: department_course_section_classroom
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  s.sec_id AS sec_id,
  s.semester AS semester,
  s.year AS year,
  s.building AS building,
  s.room_number AS room_number,
  cl.capacity AS capacity
FROM department d
JOIN course c ON c.dept_name = d.dept_name
JOIN section s ON s.course_id = c.course_id
LEFT JOIN classroom cl ON cl.building = s.building AND cl.room_number = s.room_number

params.description: Provides classroom assignment and capacity for each course section (one row per section identified by course, sec_id, semester, year) along with the department name.
params.when_to_use: Find which building/room and its capacity is assigned to a specific course section (by course_id, sec_id, semester, year). | List all sections for a department including their assigned classroom and capacity. | Compose higher-level aggregations about sections by classroom or department when the section is the analytic grain (e.g., count sections per room, average capacity for sections). | Serve as a canonical section-level source when joining section attributes with classroom attributes (capacity).
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name for the course — derived from department.dept_name (joined via course.dept_name). | course_id: identifier for the course — derived from course.course_id (base column). | sec_id: section identifier within a course — derived from section.sec_id (base column). | semester: semester identifier for the section (e.g., Fall, Spring) — derived from section.semester (base column). | year: year for the section offering — derived from section.year (base column). | building: building assigned to the section — derived from section.building (base column). May be NULL if not assigned. | room_number: room number assigned to the section — derived from section.room_number (base column). May be NULL if not assigned. | capacity: seating capacity of the assigned classroom — derived from classroom.capacity (base column). NULL when no matching classroom row exists (LEFT JOIN).
params.grounded_columns: department.dept_name | course.course_id | course.dept_name | section.sec_id | section.semester | section.year | section.building | section.room_number | classroom.building | classroom.room_number | classroom.capacity
params.metric: capacity = classroom.capacity  -- direct passthrough of the classroom.capacity column (no aggregation).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base on dept_name — safe because department_base is one-row-per-department (joining on department.dept_name will not multiply section rows). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to course (or a view normalized to one-row-per-course) on course_id — safe because course is one-row-per-course; joining preserves one row per section as this view already has one row per section linked to exactly one course. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to classroom_base on (building, room_number) — safe because classroom_base is one-row-per-classroom; joining will not duplicate section rows and preserves capacity as a section-level attribute. | do NOT join without care to one-to-many/detail tables (e.g., a hypothetical enrollments or meeting_times table) directly to this view unless you either aggregate those detail rows first or intend to produce multiple rows per section. Such joins will multiply rows and any derived per-section measures (like capacity) unless you re-aggregate (e.g., sum, avg) after the join. | do NOT join to views that are one-to-many with respect to section (for example, a view that lists multiple instructors per section or multiple meeting times per section) unless you (a) join on keys that preserve a 1:1 relationship, or (b) pre-aggregate the many-side to one row per section (e.g., string_agg of instructors or count of meetings). | When composing aggregations: if you aggregate this view up (e.g., count sections per building), compute aggregates from this view directly. If you need measures from both this view and another many-sided view, aggregate the many-sided view to the same grain (section or a coarser grain) before joining to avoid double-counting. | Primary key / grain note: this view is at grain ['section.course_id','section.sec_id','section.semester','section.year'] — treat it as one-row-per-section. Any join that respects that grain (joins to one-row-per-department, one-row-per-course, one-row-per-classroom) is safe; joins to tables that have multiple rows per that section will require re-aggregation.

views.name: dept_course_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.dept_name AS dept_name,
  COUNT(*) AS dept_course_count
FROM
  course AS c
GROUP BY
  c.dept_name

params.description: Counts the number of courses per department (one row per department name).
params.when_to_use: Get the number of courses offered by each department (dept_name -> course count). | Compose departmental course counts into higher-level reports (e.g., join with department metadata to show names, budgets, or building info). | Filter or rank departments by course count (e.g., find top departments by number of courses). | Serve as an aggregated input when computing ratios or rates that use courses-per-department as the numerator or denominator.
params.output_schema: dept_name: department name used as the grouping key; derived from course.dept_name | dept_course_count: count of course rows for that dept_name; derived from COUNT(*) over course rows
params.metric: dept_course_count = COUNT(*)  -- aggregate computed over rows in course grouped by course.dept_name
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base (or departments_rowlevel or department_budget_stats) on department_base.dept_name = dept_course_counts.dept_name — safe because dept_course_counts has one row per dept_name, so joining by dept_name to a single-row-per-department dimension will not duplicate the aggregated course count. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dept_top_instructor_rank or instructors_by_dept on dept_name when those sibling views are one-row-per-department (or have been pre-aggregated to one row per dept_name). If the sibling view is one-row-per-dept, the join will not duplicate dept_course_count. | do NOT directly join dept_course_counts to a one-to-many detail table/view such as section_room_assignment or classroom_base without re-aggregation first — e.g., joining to section_room_assignment (many sections per dept or course) would multiply dept_course_count because dept_course_counts is aggregated at department level and the detail side can have multiple rows per department. If you need combined metrics with such detail tables, either: | - re-aggregate the detail side to one row per dept_name before joining (e.g., count sections per dept), or | - join first at the detail level to course, then re-aggregate both measures together at the desired grain. | When joining to building_classroom_counts, classroom_capacity_by_building, or classroom-related sibling views: ensure you join on a departmental key (dept_name) only if those views have been reduced to one row per dept_name; otherwise, aggregate the classroom-side to dept_name first. Joins on building identifiers will generally not align with dept_name and will require an explicit mapping table or intermediate join (e.g., department -> building) to avoid accidental duplication. | General rule: this view is strictly one-row-per-course-department-name. It is safe to join (without re-aggregation) only to other datasets that are also one-row-per-department-name (same key). If joining to many-side datasets, either re-aggregate the many-side to dept_name or perform joins at the base-table level and then compute aggregates together to preserve correct counts.
