views.name: teaches_with_section_timeplace
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.ID,
  t.course_id,
  t.sec_id,
  t.semester,
  t.year,
  s.building,
  s.room_number,
  s.time_slot_id
FROM teaches AS t
LEFT JOIN section_room_assignment AS s
  ON t.course_id = s.course_id
  AND t.sec_id = s.sec_id
  AND t.semester = s.semester
  AND t.year = s.year

params.description: Provides section-level assignment of classroom time/place for each teaches record (which instructor-course-section meeting is assigned to a building/room/time slot).
params.when_to_use: Find the classroom (building, room) and time slot associated with a particular course section taught by an instructor (by ID, course_id, sec_id, semester, year). | Filter or group instructor teaching records by classroom attributes (building, room_number, time_slot_id). | Compose section-level queries that need classroom location or time_slot information joined to the teaches relation without changing the teaches grain.
params.output_schema: ID: instructor assignment identifier from teaches.ID (teaches.ID) — the primary identifier of the teaches row returned by the view. | course_id: course identifier from teaches.course_id (teaches.course_id) — identifies which course the section is for. | sec_id: section identifier from teaches.sec_id (teaches.sec_id) — identifies the section within the course. | semester: semester label from teaches.semester (teaches.semester) — academic term of the section. | year: year from teaches.year (teaches.year) — academic year of the section. | building: building identifier/name from section_room_assignment.building (section_room_assignment.building) — the building assigned to the section, NULL if no assignment. | room_number: room number from section_room_assignment.room_number (section_room_assignment.room_number) — the room assigned to the section, NULL if no assignment. | time_slot_id: time slot identifier from section_room_assignment.time_slot_id (section_room_assignment.time_slot_id) — the scheduled time slot for the section, NULL if no assignment.
params.grounded_columns: teaches.ID | teaches.course_id | teaches.sec_id | teaches.semester | teaches.year | section_room_assignment.building | section_room_assignment.room_number | section_room_assignment.time_slot_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or lookup views/tables keyed 1:1 to the view's grain (teaches keyed by ID OR by the composite key (course_id, sec_id, semester, year)): join to instructors_by_dept on teaches.ID = instructors_by_dept.ID — safe because instructors_by_dept is expected to be one-row-per-instructor-assignment (no duplication of teaches rows). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to department_base on course_id (e.g., output.course_id = department_base.course_id) only if department_base is one-row-per-course; safe when that dimension is 1:1 to course_id so teaches rows are not multiplied. | DO NOT join directly to any table/view that is one-to-many relative to this view's grain without re-aggregation, because such joins will duplicate rows/measures. Examples to avoid unless you aggregate first: building_classroom_counts (if it is aggregated by building but includes multiple rows per building and you join by building without aggregation), classroom_locations_distinct (which may list multiple locations per room), or section_room_assignment if used again at a finer grain — these can multiply rows. | If you need to combine with one-to-many child data (e.g., multiple classroom events per section or multiple metrics per time_slot), first aggregate that child table to the view's grain (ID or the composite key course_id+sec_id+semester+year) and then join the aggregated result. For example, to attach a count of room-events per section, compute COUNT(*) grouped by (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) from the child table, then join on those keys — this preserves cardinality-safe measures. | When composing additional joins, prefer joining on the view's natural keys: (ID) for instructor-assignment-level joins or the composite key (course_id, sec_id, semester, year) for section-level joins. Those keys preserve the view's grain and avoid accidental duplication.
